m. The I–V characteristic of
the wire is shown.

What is the resistivity of the metal from which the wire is made?

hints: Notice the graph is $I$ against $V$ with $I = 5.0 \, \text{A}$ at $V = 10 \, \text{V}$, so resistance must be found from $R = V/I$, not the gradient $I/V$.
Recall $\rho = RA/L$ for the $0.80 \, \text{m}$ wire, so you need the cross-sectional area from the diameter $5.0 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m}$.
Convert diameter to radius $r = 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m}$ before using $A = \pi r^2$, then multiply by $R$ and divide by $L$ and check $\Omega \text{m}$.
walkthrough: Read resistance from the straight-line $I$-$V$ graph. At $V = 10 \, \text{V}$, $I = 5.0 \, \text{A}$, so $R = V/I = 10/5.0 = 2.0 \, \Omega$. The same ratio at $V = 5.0 \, \text{V}$, $I = 2.5 \, \text{A}$ confirms it.

Find the cross-sectional area from the diameter $d = 5.0 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m}$. Radius is $r = d/2 = 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \, \text{m}$, so $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (2.5 \times 10^{-4})^2 \approx 1.96 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}^2$.
Calculate: $2.0 \times 1.96 \times 10^{-7} = 3.93 \times 10^{-7}$, divided by $0.80$ gives $\approx 4.9 \times 10^{-7} \, \Omega \text{m}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 4, consistent with using diameter instead of radius when finding $A = \pi r^2$.

B.explanation: Too small, consistent with an error in area or in reading resistance as $I/V$ instead of $V/I$ combined with rounding.

C.explanation: Gives $R = 2.0 \, \Omega$ from the graph and $\rho = RA/L \approx 4.9 \times 10^{-7} \, \Omega \text{m}$.

D.explanation: Too large by a factor of about 4, consistent with using diameter as radius so area is 4 times too large.
